presentingComplaint: High fever with rigors and confusion, now cold and clammy with a low blood pressure not responding to fluids.
history: 3-day history of fever, dysuria and left flank pain, worsening over the last 12 hours with rigors, reduced urine output and drowsiness. Type 2 diabetic on metformin; prior episode of urinary tract infection. Brought to ED by family who report progressive confusion since morning. No recent hospitalization or antibiotics. No known drug allergies.
examination: Toxic-looking, drowsy (GCS 13, E3V4M6), peripherally cold with mottled knees and prolonged capillary refill (>3s). Left costovertebral angle tenderness. Chest clear, no murmur, abdomen soft with no peritonism. No focal neurological deficit, no neck stiffness, no rash.
imaging: Bedside USS: left hydronephrosis with echogenic debris suggestive of obstructed infected system; CT KUB advised to exclude obstructing calculus.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures and urine culture sent before antibiotics; Gram-negative bacilli reported on urine Gram stain (culture pending).
finalDiagnosis: Septic shock secondary to obstructive urosepsis (Gram-negative source)
citations: Harrison 22e — Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock
Surviving Sepsis Campaign: Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021
stewardship: Broad-spectrum empiric IV antibiotics within 1 hour after cultures: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV (loading dose, then renally adjusted) covering Enterobacterales for community urosepsis; escalate to a carbapenem if ESBL risk. Concurrent source control with urgent urological decompression (ureteric stent or nephrostomy) of the obstructed infected system. De-escalate on culture and sensitivities.
contraindications: Penicillin/beta-lactam allergy (use aztreonam + aminoglycoside or carbapenem depending on cross-reactivity)
Acute kidney injury — renal dose-adjust and avoid/limit nephrotoxic aminoglycosides
Avoid further metformin during AKI (lactic acidosis risk)
edgeCases: Warm vasodilated 'flash' presentation can mask early shock — normal-appearing extremities do not exclude it
Relative adrenal insufficiency: add hydrocortisone if pressor-refractory
Obstructed pyelonephritis will not respond to antibiotics alone — source control (decompression) is essential
expectedMaiK: This is septic shock — persistent hypotension requiring vasopressors to keep MAP >=65 mmHg plus lactate >2 mmol/L despite adequate fluid resuscitation, most likely from an obstructed urinary source. Prioritise the Surviving Sepsis 1-hour bundle: cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg crystalloid, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and noradrenaline for refractory hypotension, alongside urgent urological source control.
expectedNextQuestions: Has MAP responded to a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, or is a vasopressor already needed?
Any history of renal stones, prior ESBL organism, or recent instrumentation?
expectedInvestigations: Serial lactate clearance and repeat blood cultures
CT KUB / urgent urological imaging to confirm and relieve obstruction
regressionAssertions: vasopressorRequirement + lactateElevated + hypotension must not resolve to uncomplicated SEPSIS or PYELONEPHRITIS
